Usage: go2cs [options] <input> [output_dir]

Common options:
  -recurse[=module,nuget]  Convert a module and its third-party dependencies (=module: the module
                           only; =nuget: standard library from NuGet)
  -go2cspath <dir>         Where the go2cs standard library and runtime are, when they are not from
                           NuGet (env GO2CSPATH)
  -platforms <os/arch>     The target platform, os/arch (default: this machine's)
  -tags <list>             Build tags applied when loading packages, comma-separated
  -comments                Carry the Go source comments into the C#
  -stdlib                  Convert the Go standard library itself, or the packages named after it
  -cgo                     Convert a cgo package whose C use go2cs can bind (needs a C compiler)
  -tests                   Also convert the package's Go tests and emit a runnable C# test host
  -test-action <action>    With -tests: convert, build, run, compare (with go test) or all
  -version                 Print the converter's release tuple and exit

Examples:
  go2cs package_dir out                        convert one package
  go2cs -recurse=nuget module_dir out          convert a module, with the standard library from NuGet
  go2cs -tests -test-action all pkg_dir out    convert a package and its tests, run them, compare with go test
  go2cs -stdlib fmt strings                    convert standard library packages

go2cs -help all lists every option. go2cs -help <option> explains one, for example go2cs -help tests.
go2cs toolchain -help manages the Go toolchain go2cs converts with.
The full reference is docs/CommandLine.md in the go2cs repository.
